author: Dark916
quote: When I heard GTA 6 was launching at a $100 price point, I expected an incredible game. Instead, after 9 hours of playtime, I have zero desire to pick it back **** graphics and core gameplay mechanics are genuinely great, but the story completely ruins the experience. I couldn't stand the female lead—the more I learned about her backstory, the less I liked her—and the male lead feels completely basic, acting like a passive sidekick who just follows her orders.Gameplay-wise, it feels like an unfocused mashup of Red Dead Redemption 2, The Sims, and GTA. Save your money and skip this one—it’s just not worth your time.

author: Dark916
quote: Age of Empires III holds a very special place in my heart as my number one favorite multiplayer game of all time. I’ve logged well over 3,000 hours into it, and back in its prime, I would spend 4 to 8 hours straight locked into intense online matches. The campaign is a nice bonus with a solid story, but the multiplayer is where this game truly shines. The graphics and mechanics aren't perfect, so I can't give it a 9 or a 10, but it is easily a solid 8 out of 10. What ultimately killed it for me was the lack of ongoing developer support. Watching the devs shift their focus almost entirely to Age of Empires II and IV felt like the AoE III community was just kicked to the curb, which is why I eventually stopped playing online. While the multiplayer base is pretty small nowadays, I still recommend picking it up for the single-player campaign—especially since you can get it fairly cheap. And if you can manage to find a multiplayer match, definitely give it a shot.
game_title: Age of Empires III: Definitive Edition

author: Dark916
quote: Medieval II: Total War is a fantastic game. While the graphics are definitely showing their age, it remains one of my most-played titles on Steam, where I’ve put in nearly 900 hours. Do I recommend it? Absolutely. Will it take some time to learn the mechanics? Yes, and the dated controls are really the only major flaw keeping it from perfection. Is it worth it? 100%. While the base game is good on its own, what really carries this title to the next level is its incredible modding community. The vast majority of my playtime has been spent playing Lord of the Rings overhaul mods (like Third Age). Getting to play a grand-strategy Total War game set in Middle-earth is the primary reason I love this game so much and have logged so many hours in it. I would love to see Creative Assembly release an updated version or remade entry someday, but even as it stands, it’s a solid 9 out of 10 that every strategy fan should check out.

author: Dark916
quote: Pokémon Legends: Arceus is a great game that truly captures the magic of the anime's "gotta catch 'em all" spirit, making you actually want to go out into the wild and complete the Pokédex. Game Freak took a bold risk trying something new here, and it pays off as a fantastic alternative genre alongside the mainline series. Having the central town dynamically expand and improve as you complete side quests was a really rewarding feature that made the world feel alive. While the action-oriented battle system could still use some refinement, the real downside was the distinct lack of trainer battles throughout the region—there simply wasn't enough battling overall. The environments could have also used more detail, though some of those visual constraints were likely due to hardware limits. Overall, despite a few flaws, it stands as a strong 8 out of 10.

author: Dark916
quote: Pokémon Sword and Shield (User Score: 7.0/10): Pokémon Sword and Shield is a solid 7 out of 10 entry with a fun story, though its overall progression is way too linear and the main region feels overly confined. Its absolute best feature is the Gym system, where packed, sports-arena-style venues combined with Dynamaxing make every major battle feel grand and exciting. The game also features a great rival in Hop, whose struggle with self-doubt after repeated losses gives him genuine character growth. On the downside, the villainous factions are completely disappointing annoyances, the post-game Champion Cup lacks randomized variety, and the Frankenstein-style Fossil Pokémon are easily some of the worst designs in the franchise. The DLC areas offer good content, but the campaign pacing would have benefited greatly from a mandatory training detour to the Isle of Armor mid-game rather than saving it for later. Ultimately, the post-game quest with Sordward and Shielbert feels like a tedious chore, and handing out Legendary Pokémon at the end of the DLC without deeper side-story integration feels rushed.

author: Dark916
quote: Pokémon Brilliant Diamond and Shining Pearl (User Score: 4.0/10): Pokémon Brilliant Diamond and Shining Pearl are some of the most awful remakes in the franchise. Instead of modernizing the Sinnoh region, ILCA basically did a lazy one-to-one port of the original Diamond and Pearl with a slight visual update. The chibi art style looks terrible, and the game would have been drastically better if they had gone with the Let's Go, Pikachu! visual style instead. They completely failed to fix the broken Pokédex from the originals, leaving players with a severely limited selection of Fire-type Pokémon. Worse yet, they ignored all the story and gameplay improvements introduced in Pokémon Platinum. When you compare these games to top-tier remakes like HeartGold/SoulSilver or Omega Ruby/Alpha Sapphire, BDSP fails on almost every level. I cannot recommend buying this game unless you find it deeply discounted on sale.

author: Dark916
quote: Pokémon Scarlet and Violet is an okay RPG, but it is definitely not a 10 out of 10. It’s not an A-plus, and I wouldn't even call it a B-plus. It isn't an F, but I couldn't even give it a D either. Honestly, pushing it to a 7 is hard—if I'm being real, it’s more of a 6 out of 10. The Pokémon designs and movesets are great, and I actually really liked the Terastalizing mechanics and how they worked in battle. However, how they used Tera in the gym battles was awful. Having a Normal-type like Teddiursa in a Bug gym just felt off. It would have been much cooler if Gym Leaders used Tera defensively—like if you bring a Fire-type into a Grass gym, the leader counters you with a Water Tera-type using Tera Blast. The visuals definitely could have been better, though I picked up the game late in its run rather than playing on launch day. The Legendary Pokémon looked cool, but they didn't feel like they had any real impact on the world or environment. Team Star was also uninteresting—they're just a bunch of kids who got bullied and became bullies themselves. A villain group acting like a real threat trying to take down the academy would have been way more interesting, but Game Freak didn't push the story that far. The Elite Four in the main story was another big letdown. Being quizzed on what you liked about each gym was terrible; the members were weak choices, and having Larry serve as both a Gym Leader and an Elite Four member felt lazy. As for the DLC, the initial story was fine, but once it moved to Blueberry Academy, it completely fell flat. If they had added eight new gyms and a whole new Elite Four to that second school, it would have been perfect.

author: Dark916
quote: Grand Theft Auto IV has one of the absolute best stories in the entire franchise. Following Niko Bellic—a guy running from his dark past with the mafia, coming to America for a fresh start, only to get dragged right back into the criminal underworld—makes for an incredibly grounded and compelling campaign. The map progression follows that classic, rewarding GTA formula where opening up each new section of the city feels earned as you work your way up. It definitely retains that iconic classic GTA vibe. You even get to hang out and do side activities around Liberty City with your cousin Roman, which adds a lot of personality to the experience. While the graphics are undeniably dated by today's standards, the narrative more than makes up for it. Does the story beat San Andreas? Not quite, but the visuals and physics are a clear step up from the PS2 era. Overall, I’d give the story an incredible 9 out of 10. If you haven't experienced Niko's journey yet, it is an absolute must-play—I think any fan of the series will love it.

author: Dark916
quote: Grand Theft Auto V is a fantastic game. I’ve beaten the story three times now—first back on the Xbox 360/PS4 era—and it holds up incredibly **** campaign is top-tier, and Trevor easily stands out as one of the best characters in the game. Beyond the main story, the world map is massive, the side quests are genuinely interesting, and the heist setups are a total highlight. On top of that, the vehicle selection and customisation options give you plenty of freedom to mess around in San Andreas.While GTA Online isn't really my thing and can be more of a pain than it's worth, the single-player mode is where the game truly shines. Is it the absolute best game in the series? Graphically, it definitely takes the crown. Storytelling-wise, it’s right up there, though I’d still rank it in my top three alongside GTA IV and San **** you somehow haven't played through the single-player campaign yet, it’s an absolute must-play. Easily a 9 out of 10

author: Dark916
quote: I haven't played The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time since back on the N64, so when I came back to play this release, I wasn't sure what to expect. But after putting about a day's worth of play into it, it’s easily the best way to experience the **** visual overhaul is incredible—every town and location has been revamped with far more detail and atmosphere, bringing the world to life while keeping the soul of the original intact. Some major quality-of-life changes make getting around much smoother, like the improved flow around the lake area and when you first enter Lon Lon Ranch. Plus, fixing the old Water Temple soft-lock issue means you no longer have to worry about bricking a save and resetting your **** music hits just as hard as ever—even right when I booted it up on the title screen, I caught myself saying, "That sound hits hard." Overall, this is an absolute must-play game for both returning N64 players and newcomers alike
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Dark916
quote:
Unicorn Overlord is a fun tactical RPG, but it suffers from a few repetitive elements.
The Good: Great gameplay that reminds me of Fire Emblem, an enjoyable story, and plenty of content (it took me over 60 hours to clear with side quests).
The Bad: The battles start to feel repetitive as you go, and enemy design lacks variety—the undead units are essentially just reskins.
Verdict: A strong 8/10 title. Definitely worth picking up if you're between games and need something fun to sink some time into.

author: Dark916
quote:
Metroid Prime Remastered is a masterpiece that holds up amazingly well.
The Gameplay & Map: Classic Metroidvania design at its finest. The map size is perfect, and backtracking to open previously locked doors with new upgrades is super rewarding.
Graphics & Story: The visuals are top-notch, and the developers wisely kept the original story and experience completely unchanged.
Verdict: Whether you played it back on the GameCube or are jumping in for the first time on Switch 2, this is a must-play. Highly recommended!

author: Dark916
quote:
Rating: 7/10Metroid Prime 4: Beyond is a decent experience, but it’s hard to justify paying full price.
The Good: The graphics are absolutely incredible and easily the strong point of the game.
The Bad: The open-world areas are boring, and the map design feels surprisingly small and linear compared to the original Metroid Prime.
The Story: The narrative is a mixed bag. The game introduces NPCs that are hard to get attached to, making the developers' attempted fake-out deaths feel unearned.
Verdict: Worth picking up on sale for $40, but not a full-price buy.

author: Dark916
quote: Pokémon Legends: Z-A is a major disappointment and doesn't justify its $60–$70 price tag, especially with its overpriced DLC. While the increased focus on battling is a step in the right direction, it doesn't save the game from its flaws. Compared to Pokémon Legends: Arceus, the experience falls short in three main areas. First, the AI is frustrating; enemies target the trainer more than the Pokémon. Second, the catching system was perfected in Arceus, and the changes made here are a downgrade. Finally, the map feels small and claustrophobic rather than open-world, and the graphics are surprisingly poor. Ultimately, Arceus remains the far superior title
